title.zh: 卷六十七 列傳第五十五: 崔彥穆 楊纂 段永 令狐整 唐永 柳敏 王士良
title.en: Volume 67 Biographies 55: Cui Yanmu, Yang Zuan, Duan Yong, Ling Huzheng, Tang Yong, Liu Min, Wang Shiliang
title.raw: 卷六十七 列傳第五十五: 崔彥穆 楊纂 段永 令狐整 唐永 柳敏 王士良 Volume 67 Biographies 55: Cui Yanmu, Yang Zuan, Duan Yong, Ling Huzheng, Tang Yong, Liu Min, Wang Shiliang

sentences.zh: 崔彥穆 楊纂 段永 令狐整 唐永 柳敏 王士良

translations.literal: Cui Yanmu, Yang Zuan, Duan Yong, Ling Huzheng, Tang Yong, Liu Min, Wang Shiliang
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yanmu, Yang Zuan, Duan Yong, Ling Huzheng, Tang Yong, Liu Min, and Wang Shiliang

sentences.zh: 列傳第五十五

translations.literal: Biographies, number fifty-five
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 55

sentences.zh: 崔彥穆楊纂段永令狐整子熙唐永子瑾柳敏子昂王士良

translations.literal: Cui Yanmu, Yang Zuan, Duan Yong, Ling Huzheng and his son Xi, Tang Yong and his son Jin, Liu Min and his son Ang, Wang Shiliang
translations.idiomatic: This chapter treats Cui Yanmu, Yang Zuan, Duan Yong, Ling Huzheng (and his son Xi), Tang Yong (and his son Jin), Liu Min (and his son Ang), and Wang Shiliang.

sentences.zh: 崔彥穆，字彥穆，清河東武城人，魏司空安陽侯林之九世孫也。

translations.literal: Cui Yanmu, styled Yanmu, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe commandery, a ninth-generation descendant of Lin, Marquis of Anyang and Wei Director of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yanmu, who also used Yanmu as his style name, came from Dongwucheng in Qinghe. He was a ninth-generation descendant of Cui Lin, Marquis of Anyang and Wei Director of Works.

sentences.zh: 曾祖顗，後魏平東府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yan was a consulting staff officer in the Eastern Office of Northern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yan had served as a consulting staff officer in the Eastern Office under Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖蔚，遭從兄司徒浩之難，南奔江左。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wei, caught up in the trouble of his cousin the Minister of Works Hao, fled south across the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wei, implicated in the troubles of his cousin Minister of Works Hao, fled south to the lands beyond the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 仕宋，為給事黃門侍郎、汝南義陽二郡守。

translations.literal: He served the Song, becoming Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Supervisor of the Secretariat, and prefect of Runan and Yiyang commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liu Song he rose to Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Supervisor of the Secretariat, and held the prefectures of Runan and Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 延興初，復歸於魏，拜潁川郡守，因家焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yanxing era he returned to Wei, was appointed prefect of Yingchuan commandery, and settled his family there.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yanxing era he returned to Northern Wei, was made prefect of Yingchuan, and established his household there.

sentences.zh: 後終於郢州刺史。

translations.literal: He later died in office as inspector of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He later ended his career as inspector of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父幼，位終永昌郡守。

translations.literal: His father You ended his career as prefect of Yongchang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father You served until he reached the post of prefect of Yongchang commandery.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，以獻皇后外曾祖，追贈上開府儀同三司、新州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang in Sui, because he was the Empress Dowager Xian's maternal great-grandfather, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Senior General of the Upper Palace with the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies and made inspector of Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Kaihuang reign, because he was the maternal great-grandfather of Empress Dowager Xian, he was posthumously granted the rank of Senior General of the Upper Palace with the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies and the title of inspector of Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 彥穆幼明悟。

translations.literal: Yanmu was clever from childhood.
translations.idiomatic: Yanmu showed exceptional intelligence even as a boy.

sentences.zh: 神彩卓然。

translations.literal: His bearing was outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: His presence was strikingly distinguished.

sentences.zh: 魏吏部尚書隴西李神亻雋，有知人之鑒，見而歎曰：「王佐才也。

translations.literal: Li Shenjun of Longxi, Minister of Personnel of Wei, had a discerning eye for men; when he saw Yanmu he sighed and said, "This is talent fit to assist a king.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenjun of Longxi, who was Wei Minister of Personnel and renowned for judging character, met Yanmu and exclaimed, "Here is a man fit to stand at a ruler's right hand.

sentences.zh: 」永安末，除司徒府參軍事，再遷大司馬從事中郎。

translations.literal: " At the end of the Yong'an era he was appointed staff officer in the Secretariat, and was twice promoted to Attendant Gentleman in the Grand Marshal's office.
translations.idiomatic: " Late in the Yong'an era he entered the Secretariat as a staff officer, and was soon promoted twice to Attendant Gentleman in the Grand Marshal's office.

sentences.zh: 孝武西遷，彥穆時不得從。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Yanmu was unable to follow at the time.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu withdrew to the west, Yanmu could not accompany him at once.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，乃與兄彥珍于成皋舉義，因攻拔滎陽，禽東魏郡守蘇淑。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong he and his elder brother Yanzhen raised a loyal force at Chenggao, captured Xingyang, and took prisoner Su Shu, the Eastern Wei prefect of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong he joined his elder brother Yanzhen in raising arms at Chenggao, seized Xingyang, and captured Su Shu, the Eastern Wei commandery prefect.

sentences.zh: 仍與鄉郡王元洪威攻潁川，斬其刺史李景遺。

translations.literal: He then joined Wang Yuanhongwei of his native commandery in attacking Yingchuan and beheaded its inspector Li Jingyi.
translations.idiomatic: He next allied with Wang Yuanhongwei of his home commandery to assault Yingchuan and executed its inspector Li Jingyi.

sentences.zh: 即拜滎陽郡守，尋賜爵千乘縣侯。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed prefect of Xingyang commandery and soon enfeoffed as Marquis of Qiansheng county.
translations.idiomatic: He was promptly made prefect of Xingyang and shortly thereafter enfeoffed as Marquis of Qiansheng.

sentences.zh: 十四年，授散騎常侍、司農卿。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Regular Attendant and Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he received the posts of Regular Attendant and Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 時軍國草創，眾務殷繁，周文乃引彥穆入幕府，兼掌文翰。

translations.literal: At that time the state and army were newly founded and affairs were pressing; Emperor Wen of Zhou brought Yanmu into his staff and also had him oversee documents.
translations.idiomatic: With the state and army still being organized and business overwhelming, Emperor Wen of Zhou drew Yanmu into his staff and entrusted him with written work as well.

sentences.zh: 及於謹伐江陵，彥穆以本官從平之。

translations.literal: When Yu Jin campaigned against Jiangling, Yanmu accompanied him in his original office and took part in the pacification.
translations.idiomatic: During Yu Jin's campaign against Jiangling, Yanmu went in his existing capacity and shared in the victory.

sentences.zh: 周明帝初，進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming of Zhou's reign he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and General of the Upper Palace with the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Emperor Ming of Zhou he was advanced to General of Agile Cavalry and General of the Upper Palace with the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 俄拜安州刺史，總管十二州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed inspector of An Prefecture and commander-in-chief of military affairs in twelve prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became inspector of An Prefecture and overall commander of military affairs across twelve prefectures.

sentences.zh: 入為禦正大夫。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Grand Master of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as Grand Master of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 陳氏請敦鄰好。

translations.literal: The Chen state requested friendly relations with neighboring states.
translations.idiomatic: Chen sought to renew cordial ties with its neighbors.

sentences.zh: 詔彥穆使焉。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Yanmu envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Yanmu to serve as envoy.

sentences.zh: 彥穆風韻閑曠，器度方雅，善玄言，解談謔，甚為江表所稱。

translations.literal: Yanmu's manner was leisurely and open, his capacity square and elegant; he was skilled in arcane discourse and witty conversation, and was greatly praised in the lands south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Yanmu carried himself with unhurried ease and measured grace, excelled in philosophical talk and repartee, and won high esteem throughout the lower Yangtze region.

sentences.zh: 轉戶部中大夫，進爵為公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of the Household Revenue and advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Grand Master of the Household Revenue and raised to ducal rank.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，聘齊還，除金州刺史，總管七州諸軍事，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe, returning from an embassy to Qi, he was appointed inspector of Jin Prefecture, commander-in-chief of military affairs in seven prefectures, and advanced to the rank of Great General.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianhe, after an embassy to Northern Qi, he became inspector of Jin Prefecture, commander-in-chief over seven prefectures, and was promoted to Great General.

sentences.zh: 尋徵拜小司徒。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned and appointed Junior Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and named Junior Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝崩，隋文帝輔政，三方起兵，以彥穆為行軍總管，與襄州總管王誼討司馬消難。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan died and Emperor Wen of Sui acted as regent, the three regions rose in arms; Yanmu was made campaigning commander-in-chief and, with Xiang Prefecture commander-in-chief Wang Yi, marched against Sima Xiaonan.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xuan's death, when Emperor Wen of Sui took power as regent and rebellion broke out on three fronts, Yanmu was appointed campaigning commander-in-chief and, together with Wang Yi, commander-in-chief of Xiang Prefecture, moved to suppress Sima Xiaonan.

sentences.zh: 軍次荊州，總管獨孤永業有異志，遂收而戮之。

translations.literal: When the army reached Jing Prefecture, the commander-in-chief Dugu Yongye harbored disloyal intent, so Yanmu seized and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: As the army halted at Jing Prefecture, the regional commander Dugu Yongye showed signs of treason, and Yanmu had him arrested and put to death.

sentences.zh: 及事平，隋文帝徵王誼入朝，即以彥穆為襄州刺史，總管六州諸軍事，加授上大將軍，進爵東郡公。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Emperor Wen of Sui summoned Wang Yi to court and appointed Yanmu inspector of Xiang Prefecture, commander-in-chief of military affairs in six prefectures, additionally granting him the rank of Senior Great General and advancing his enfeoffment to Duke of Dongjun.
translations.idiomatic: Once order was restored, Emperor Wen summoned Wang Yi to the capital and gave Yanmu the inspectorship of Xiang Prefecture, command over six prefectures, the additional rank of Senior Great General, and advancement to Duke of Dongjun.

sentences.zh: 頃之，永業家自理得雪，彥穆坐除名。

translations.literal: Before long Yongye's family cleared themselves and Yanmu was punished by removal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Yongye's kin proved their innocence, and Yanmu was stripped of rank and office.

sentences.zh: 尋復官爵。

translations.literal: Soon his offices and enfeoffment were restored.
translations.idiomatic: His titles and posts were soon restored.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Kaihuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Kaihuang.

sentences.zh: 子君綽嗣。

translations.literal: His son Junchuo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Junchuo inherited his line.

sentences.zh: 君綽性夷簡，博覽經史，有父風。

translations.literal: Junchuo's nature was mild and simple; he read widely in the classics and histories and had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Junchuo was easygoing and unassuming, steeped himself in the classics and histories, and bore his father's stamp.

sentences.zh: 大象末，丞相府賓曹參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daxiang era he was a staff officer in the Chancellor's Bureau of Guests.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Daxiang era he served as a staff officer in the Chancellor's Bureau of Guests.

sentences.zh: 君綽弟君肅，解巾道王侍讀，大象末，潁川郡守。

translations.literal: Junchuo's younger brother Junsu first took office as tutor to the Prince of Dao, and at the end of Daxiang was prefect of Yingchuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Junchuo's younger brother Junsu began as tutor to the Prince of Dao and, by the close of Daxiang, was prefect of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 楊纂，廣寧人也，父安仁，魏朔州鎮將。

translations.literal: Yang Zuan was a native of Guangning; his father Anren was a garrison general of Shuozhou in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zuan came from Guangning. His father Anren had been a garrison general at Shuozhou under Wei.

sentences.zh: 纂少慷慨有志略，勇力兼人。

translations.literal: From youth Zuan was bold and ambitious, with courage and strength surpassing ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan was high-spirited and ambitious from boyhood, and his courage and physical prowess were unmatched.

sentences.zh: 年二十，從齊神武起兵於信都，以軍功。

translations.literal: At twenty he followed Emperor Shenwu of Qi in raising troops at Xindu and won merit in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he followed Emperor Shenwu of Qi when he raised his banner at Xindu and distinguished himself in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 稍遷武州刺史。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to inspector of Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to inspector of Wu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 自以賞薄，志懷怨憤，每歎曰：「大丈夫富貴何必故鄉！

translations.literal: Finding his rewards meager, he nursed resentment in his heart and often sighed, "Must a great man win wealth in his native place?
translations.idiomatic: Believing his rewards too slight, he brooded on resentment and would often say, "Does a true man need to make his fortune in his home country?

sentences.zh: 若以妻子經懷，豈不沮人雄志！

translations.literal: If one is always thinking of wife and children, will that not choke a hero's ambition!
translations.idiomatic: If a man keeps wife and children always in mind, how can he nourish a hero's ambition!

sentences.zh: 」大統初，乃間行入關。

translations.literal: " At the beginning of Datong he made his way into the Pass by secret routes.
translations.idiomatic: " At the opening of Datong he slipped through the passes by hidden paths to join the Western Wei court.

sentences.zh: 周文執纂手曰：「人所貴者忠義也，所懼者危亡也，其能不憚危亡，蹈茲忠義者，今方見之於卿耳。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou took Zuan's hand and said, "What men prize is loyalty and righteousness; what they fear is peril and ruin. To dare peril and ruin and tread loyalty and righteousness—today I see that in you.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou clasped his hand and said, "Men value loyalty and righteousness above all and dread danger and ruin. To brave ruin for the sake of loyalty—today I see that spirit in you.

sentences.zh: 」即授征南將軍、大都督，封永興縣侯。

translations.literal: " He was immediately appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Commander, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongxing county.
translations.idiomatic: " He was at once named General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Commander, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 從周文解洛陽圍，經河橋、芒山之戰，纂每先登，軍中咸推其敢勇，累遷驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中，進爵為公，賜姓莫胡盧氏。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Wen in relieving the siege of Luoyang; in the battles at Heqiao and Mangshan he always charged first, and the army all praised his daring; he was repeatedly promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and General of the Upper Palace with the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies, made Palace Attendant, advanced to duke, and granted the surname Mohulu.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Wen in lifting the siege of Luoyang, and at Heqiao and Mangshan always led the assault, so that the whole army acclaimed his valor. He was repeatedly promoted, became General of Agile Cavalry and General of the Upper Palace with the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies, was made Palace Attendant, raised to duke, and granted the surname Mohulu.

sentences.zh: 俄授岐州刺史。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed inspector of Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made inspector of Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，進爵宋熙郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, his enfeoffment was advanced to Duke of Songxi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, his title was raised to Duke of Songxi.

sentences.zh: 保定元年，位大將軍，改封隴東郡公，除隴州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding he reached the rank of Great General, was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Longdong commandery, and appointed inspector of Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoding he attained the rank of Great General, was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Longdong, and became inspector of Long Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從隋公楊忠東伐，至并州而還。

translations.literal: He followed Duke Yang Zhong of Sui in the eastern campaign, reaching Bing Prefecture before returning.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Duke Yang Zhong of Sui on the eastern expedition as far as Bing Prefecture before turning back.

sentences.zh: 天和六年，進授柱國大將軍，轉華州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhe he was further appointed Pillar of the State and Great General and transferred to inspector of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianhe he was further advanced to Pillar of the State and Great General and transferred to Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 纂性質樸，又不識文字，前後蒞職，但推誠信而已。

translations.literal: Zuan's nature was plain and unadorned, and he could not read; in every post before and after, he governed solely by sincerity and trust.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and unlettered by nature, Zuan in every office relied on nothing but sincerity and good faith.

sentences.zh: 吏人以其忠恕，頗亦懷之。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners, because of his loyalty and forbearance, also came to cherish him.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates and people alike warmed to him for his loyalty and magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於州。

translations.literal: He soon died in that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died in office there.

sentences.zh: 子睿，位至上柱國、漁陽郡公。

translations.literal: His son Rui rose to the rank of Pillar of the State of the Upper Grade and Duke of Yuyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rui rose to Pillar of the State of the Upper Grade and Duke of Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 段永，字永賓，其先遼西石城人，晉幽州刺史疋磾之後也，曾祖愄，仕魏黃龍鎮將，因徙高陸之河陽焉。

translations.literal: Duan Yong, styled Yongbin, was descended from ancestors of Shicheng in Liaoxi; his ninth-generation ancestor was Pidi, Jin inspector of You Province; his great-grandfather Min served Wei as garrison general of Huanglong and moved his family to Heyang in Gaolu.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Yong, whose style name was Yongbin, traced his line to Shicheng in Liaoxi and was a descendant of Pidi, Jin inspector of You Province. His great-grandfather Min had been a Huanglong garrison general under Wei and resettled the family at Heyang in Gaolu.

sentences.zh: 永幼有志操，閭里稱之。

translations.literal: From childhood Yong had resolve and integrity, and his neighborhood praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy Yong showed firm purpose and integrity, and neighbors spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 魏正光末，北鎮擾亂，遂攜老幼，避地中山。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenguang era of Wei the northern garrisons were in turmoil; he then led the old and young of his household to take refuge in Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern garrisons erupted late in the Zhenguang era, he gathered the young and old of his household and fled to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 後赴洛陽，拜平東將軍，封沃陽縣伯。

translations.literal: Later he went to Luoyang and was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and enfeoffed as Earl of Woyang county.
translations.idiomatic: He later reached Luoyang, was named General Who Pacifies the East, and enfeoffed as Earl of Woyang.

sentences.zh: 青州人崔社客舉兵反，永討平之。

translations.literal: Cui Sheke of Qing Province raised troops in rebellion; Yong suppressed and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Sheke of Qing Province rebelled, Yong crushed the rising.

sentences.zh: 進爵為侯，除左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His rank was advanced to marquis and he was appointed Senior Master of Splendid Virtue of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to marquis and made Senior Master of Splendid Virtue of the Left.

sentences.zh: 時有賊魁元伯生，西自崤、潼，東至鞏、洛，屠陷城壁，所在為患。

translations.literal: At that time the bandit chieftain Yuan Bosheng, from the west from Xiao and Tong passes to the east from Gong and Luo, slaughtered and seized walled cities, and wherever he went brought disaster.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the bandit leader Yuan Bosheng ranged from the Xiao and Tong passes in the west to Gong and Luo in the east, sacking walled towns and spreading havoc wherever he marched.

sentences.zh: 孝武遣京畿大都督疋婁昭討之，昭請以五千人行。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu sent the Metropolitan Commander Piqie Zhao to suppress him; Zhao requested five thousand men for the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu dispatched Metropolitan Commander Piqie Zhao against him, and Zhao asked for five thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 永進曰：「此賊既無城柵，唯以寇抄為資，取之在速，不在眾也。

translations.literal: Yong advanced and said, "This bandit has no walled camps and relies only on raiding for sustenance; to take him depends on speed, not on numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Yong stepped forward and said, "These rebels have no fortified camps and live only by plunder. Victory lies in speed, not in massing troops.

sentences.zh: 若星馳電發，出其不虞，精騎五百足矣。

translations.literal: If we strike like a shooting star with lightning speed and catch them unprepared, five hundred elite horsemen are enough.
translations.idiomatic: If we move like a comet and take them unawares, five hundred picked horsemen will suffice.

sentences.zh: 」帝然其計，於是命永代昭，以五百騎倍道兼進，遂破平之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved his plan and therefore ordered Yong to replace Zhao; with five hundred horsemen marching day and night he broke and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted his plan, replaced Zhao with Yong, and sent five hundred horsemen on a forced march that routed and destroyed the band.

sentences.zh: 及帝西遷，永時不及從。

translations.literal: When the Emperor moved west, Yong at the time could not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor withdrew westward, Yong could not accompany him in time.

sentences.zh: 大統初，乃結宗人，潛謀歸款。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong he then joined his clansmen in a secret plan to submit allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Datong he united his kinsmen in a covert plan to return to the Western court.

sentences.zh: 密與都督趙業等襲斬西中郎將慕容顯和，傳首京師。

translations.literal: He secretly joined the commander Dugu Ye and others in a surprise attack that beheaded the Western Central Gentleman-in-Attendance Murong Xianhe and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: With Commander Zhao Ye and others he launched a surprise raid, beheaded the Western Central Gentleman-in-Attendance Murong Xianhe, and forwarded his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 以功別封昌平縣子，徐州刺史。

translations.literal: For this merit he was separately enfeoffed as Viscount of Changping county and made inspector of Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he received a separate enfeoffment as Viscount of Changping and the inspectorship of Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從禽竇泰，復弘農，破沙苑，並有戰功，進爵為公。

translations.literal: He followed in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and breaking Shaoyuan, all with battle merit, and his enfeoffment was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He shared in the capture of Dou Tai, the recovery of Hongnong, and the victory at Shaoyuan, earning battle honors each time until he was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 河橋之役，永力戰先登，授南汾州刺史。

translations.literal: In the battle at Heqiao Yong fought fiercely and charged first, and was appointed inspector of Nanfen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At Heqiao he fought with desperate valor at the head of the charge and was made inspector of Nanfen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累遷驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，賜姓爾綿氏。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and General of the Upper Palace with the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies and granted the surname Ermian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to General of Agile Cavalry and General of the Upper Palace with the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies and was granted the surname Ermian.

sentences.zh: 廢帝元年，授恆州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Fei he was appointed inspector of Heng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the deposed emperor he became inspector of Heng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 于時朝貴多其部人，謁永之日，冠蓋盈路，當時榮之。

translations.literal: At that time many court nobles were men of his native district; on days when they called on Yong, coaches and riders filled the road, and the age counted it glory.
translations.idiomatic: Many court grandees then hailed from his home region, and on days when they paid calls the road was crowded with carriages—an honor the age envied.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，進爵廣城郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, his enfeoffment was advanced to Duke of Guangcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, his title was raised to Duke of Guangcheng.

sentences.zh: 曆文、瓜二州刺史，戶部中大夫。

translations.literal: He served successively as inspector of Wen and Gua prefectures and as Grand Master of the Household Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He held the inspectorships of Wen and Gua in turn and served as Grand Master of the Household Revenue.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，拜大將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding he was appointed Great General.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Baoding he was named Great General.

sentences.zh: 永歷任內外，所在頗有聲稱，輕財好士，朝野以此重焉。

translations.literal: In every office at court and in the provinces Yong won a fair reputation; he was light with wealth and fond of scholars, and court and countryside alike honored him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Whether at court or in the provinces Yong left a solid reputation; generous with wealth and devoted to men of learning, he won esteem throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 天和四年，授小司寇。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianhe he was appointed Junior Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianhe he became Junior Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 尋為右二軍總管，率兵北道講武。

translations.literal: Soon he was made commander of the Right Second Army and led troops on the northern route for military exercises.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was commander of the Right Second Army and led troops north for war games.

sentences.zh: 遇疾，卒于賀葛城。

translations.literal: He fell ill and died at Hegge Fort.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and died at Hegge Fort.

sentences.zh: 喪遠，武帝親臨，贈使持節、柱國大將軍、同華等五州刺史，諡曰基。

translations.literal: The funeral was far away; Emperor Wu came in person; he was posthumously granted the Staff of Authority, Pillar of the State and Great General, and inspector of Tong, Hua, and four other prefectures, with the posthumous title Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Because the burial lay far off, Emperor Wu attended in person. He was posthumously granted the Staff of Authority, the rank of Pillar of the State and Great General, and the inspectorships of Tong, Hua, and four other prefectures, with the posthumous title Ji.

sentences.zh: 子岌嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ji succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 位至儀同三司、兵部下大夫。

translations.literal: He reached the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies and the post of Junior Master in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies and Junior Master in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 令狐整，字延保，敦煌人也，本名延。

translations.literal: Ling Huzheng, styled Yanbao, was a native of Dunhuang; his original name was Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Huzheng, whose style name was Yanbao, came from Dunhuang; his birth name had been Yan.

sentences.zh: 世為西士冠冕。

translations.literal: For generations his family had been the chief gentry of the western lands.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his clan had stood at the head of western gentry society.

sentences.zh: 曾祖嗣，祖紹安，官至郡守，咸為良二千石。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Si and his grandfather Shao'an both reached the rank of commandery prefect and were all worthy administrators of two-thousand-bushel rank.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Si and grandfather Shao'an had each governed a commandery and were accounted model prefects.

sentences.zh: 父虯，早以名德著聞，仕歷瓜州司馬、敦煌郡守、郢州刺史，封長城縣子。

translations.literal: His father Qiu early won renown for name and virtue; in office he served successively as Military Administrator of Gua Prefecture, prefect of Dunhuang commandery, and inspector of Ying Prefecture, and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Changcheng county.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qiu had early won fame for character and learning, and held in turn the posts of Military Administrator of Gua, prefect of Dunhuang, and inspector of Ying, with enfeoffment as Viscount of Changcheng.

sentences.zh: 魏大統末，卒於家。

translations.literal: At the end of Datong in Wei he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Datong era he died at home under Wei.

sentences.zh: 周文帝傷悼之，遣使者監護喪事，又敕鄉人為營墳壟。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou grieved for him, sent an envoy to supervise the funeral, and also ordered the people of his township to build the tomb mound.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou mourned him, dispatched an envoy to oversee the funeral, and commanded his fellow townsmen to raise the tomb mound.

sentences.zh: 贈龍驤將軍、瓜州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the rank of General of the Dragon Cavalry and inspector of Gua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named General of the Dragon Cavalry and inspector of Gua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 整幼聰敏，沈深有識量，學藝騎射並為河右所推。

translations.literal: From childhood Huzheng was clever and keen, deep and reserved with judgment; in learning, arts, and horsemanship and archery he was praised throughout the lands west of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Huzheng was clever and penetrating from boyhood, grave and far-seeing in judgment, and in scholarship, the arts, riding, and archery he was acclaimed throughout the Hexi region.

sentences.zh: 刺史魏東陽王元榮辟整為主簿，加蕩寇將軍。

translations.literal: The inspector, Prince Yuan Rong of Weidongyang, recruited Huzheng as chief clerk and additionally appointed him General Who Sweeps Away Bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan Rong of Weidongyang, then serving as prefect, took Huzheng on as chief clerk and additionally named him General Who Sweeps Away Bandits.

sentences.zh: 整進趨詳雅，對揚辯暢，謁見之際，州府傾目。

translations.literal: Huzheng's deportment in advancing was detailed and elegant, and in audience his responses were fluent; whenever he was received, the prefecture and commandery offices turned their eyes upon him.
translations.idiomatic: His bearing in court was meticulous and graceful, his replies fluent and assured; on every audience the prefectural staff watched him with admiration.

sentences.zh: 榮器整德望，嘗謂僚屬曰：「令狐延保，西州令望，方成重器，豈州郡之職所可縶維？

translations.literal: Rong valued Huzheng's virtue and reputation and once told his staff, "Linghu Yanbao is the leading figure of the western lands and is becoming a great vessel—how could a post in a prefecture or commandery hold him?
translations.idiomatic: Rong admired Huzheng's standing and once told his staff, "Linghu Yanbao is the foremost man of the west and is ripening into a pillar of state. No commandery post could possibly contain him.

sentences.zh: 但一日千里，必基武步，寡人當委以庶務，畫諾而已。

translations.literal: He travels a thousand li in a day and must first learn the martial step; I shall entrust him with routine affairs and need only initial his decisions.
translations.idiomatic: He advances a thousand li in a day and must first master the martial arts; I mean to place the daily business in his hands and simply countersign what he drafts.

sentences.zh: 」頃之，孝武西遷，河右擾亂。

translations.literal: " Before long Emperor Xiaowu moved west and the lands west of the Yellow River were in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward Emperor Xiaowu withdrew to the west, and the Hexi region fell into disorder.

sentences.zh: 榮仗整防扞，州境獲寧。

translations.literal: Rong relied on Huzheng for defense, and the prefecture's territory was kept secure.
translations.idiomatic: Rong leaned on Huzheng for defense, and the prefecture remained at peace.

sentences.zh: 及鄧彥竊據瓜州，拒不受代，整與開府張穆等密應使者申徽，執彥送京師。

translations.literal: When Deng Yan seized Gua Prefecture by force and refused to yield his post, Huzheng with the Commissioner-in-Chief Zhang Mu and others secretly supported the envoy Shen Hui, seized Yan, and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Yan seized Gua Prefecture and refused replacement, Huzheng joined Commissioner-in-Chief Zhang Mu and others in secretly aiding the envoy Shen Hui, arresting Yan and forwarding him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 周文嘉其忠節，表為都督。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou praised his loyalty and integrity and memorialized him as commander.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou commended his loyalty and recommended him as regional commander.

sentences.zh: 尋而城人張保又殺刺史成慶，與涼州刺史宇文仲和構逆，規據河西。

translations.literal: Before long the townsman Zhang Bao again killed the inspector Cheng Qing and joined the Liangzhou inspector Yuwen Zhonghe in rebellion, plotting to hold the Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the townsman Zhang Bao murdered Inspector Cheng Qing and, with Liangzhou Inspector Yuwen Zhonghe, plotted rebellion to seize the Hexi.

sentences.zh: 晉昌人呂興復害郡守郭肆，以郡應保。

translations.literal: The man of Jinchang Lü Xing again killed the commandery prefect Guo Si and offered the commandery to Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Then Lü Xing of Jinchang killed Commandery Prefect Guo Si and surrendered the commandery to Bao.

sentences.zh: 初，保等將圖為亂，慮整守義不從，既殺成慶，因欲及整。

translations.literal: At first Bao and the others intended to rebel and feared that Huzheng, holding to righteousness, would not follow; after they killed Cheng Qing they wished to strike at Huzheng as well.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's faction had first feared Huzheng's steadfast loyalty; after killing Cheng Qing they meant to destroy him too.

sentences.zh: 然人之望，復恐其下叛之，遂不敢害。

translations.literal: Yet because of the people's regard for him, they again feared that his subordinates would rebel, and therefore did not dare harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the people's esteem for Huzheng made them fear a mutiny among his followers, so they dared not touch him.

sentences.zh: 雖外加禮敬，內甚忌整。

translations.literal: Though outwardly they showed him courtesy, inwardly they greatly resented Huzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly they honored him; inwardly they hated him.

sentences.zh: 整亦偽若親附，而密欲圖之。

translations.literal: Huzheng also pretended to be close to them while secretly plotting against them.
translations.idiomatic: Huzheng in turn feigned attachment while secretly planning their ruin.

sentences.zh: 陰令所親說保曰「郡與仲和結為脣齒，令東軍漸逼涼州，彼勢孤危，恐不能敵。

translations.literal: He secretly had those close to him persuade Bao, "Your commandery and Zhonghe are lip and teeth; now the eastern army is pressing Liangzhou step by step, and their position is isolated and perilous—they may not be able to resist.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly had an ally urge Bao, "Your commandery and Zhonghe stand or fall together. The eastern army is closing on Liangzhou; isolated as they are, they may not hold.

sentences.zh: 若或摧衄，則禍及此土。

translations.literal: If they should be crushed, disaster will reach this land.
translations.idiomatic: If they are broken, this region will share their fate.

sentences.zh: 宜分遣銳師，星言救援。

translations.literal: You should detach crack troops and march to the rescue with all speed.
translations.idiomatic: Send picked troops at once to their relief.

sentences.zh: 二州合勢，則東軍可圖。

translations.literal: With the two prefectures combining their strength, the eastern army can be dealt with.
translations.idiomatic: United, the two prefectures can face the eastern army.

sentences.zh: 然後保境息人，計之上者。

translations.literal: Then your territory will be at peace and the people will rest—this is the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: Then your lands will be secure and your people at ease—the soundest course.

sentences.zh: 」保然之，而未知所任。

translations.literal: " Bao agreed but did not know whom to appoint.
translations.idiomatic: " Bao agreed but could not decide whom to send.

sentences.zh: 整又令說保曰：「曆觀成敗，在於任使，所擇不善，旋致傾危。

translations.literal: Huzheng again had them persuade Bao, "Looking through success and failure, everything turns on whom you employ; choose badly and ruin follows at once.
translations.idiomatic: Huzheng again had his man say, "Success and failure always hinge on the man chosen; the wrong commander brings instant collapse.

sentences.zh: 令狐延保兼資文武，才堪統御，若使為將，蔑不濟矣。

translations.literal: Linghu Yanbao combines civil and military gifts and has talent fit to command—if you make him general, nothing will fail.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Yanbao unites civil and military gifts and can command an army—appoint him, and you cannot fail.

sentences.zh: 」保納其計，且以整父兄等並在城中，弗之疑也，遂令整行。

translations.literal: " Bao accepted this plan, and because Huzheng's father, brothers, and the like were all in the city, he did not suspect him and therefore ordered Huzheng to march.
translations.idiomatic: " Bao took the advice; with Huzheng's kin still in the city as hostages, he suspected nothing and sent Huzheng off.

sentences.zh: 整至玉門郡，召集豪傑，說保罪逆，馳還襲之。

translations.literal: When Huzheng reached Yumen commandery he gathered the local heroes, denounced Bao's treason, and galloped back to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: At Yumen commandery Huzheng rallied the local leaders, exposed Bao's treason, and raced back to attack him.

sentences.zh: 先定晉昌，斬呂興，進軍擊保。

translations.literal: He first secured Jinchang, beheaded Lü Xing, and advanced to attack Bao.
translations.idiomatic: He secured Jinchang first, executed Lü Xing, then marched against Bao.

sentences.zh: 州人素服整威名，並棄保來附。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture had long respected Huzheng's renown and all abandoned Bao to join him.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had long revered Huzheng; all deserted Bao and rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 保遂奔吐谷渾。

translations.literal: Bao thereupon fled to Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Bao fled to Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 眾議推整為刺史。

translations.literal: The multitude proposed Huzheng as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The people urged Huzheng to become inspector.

sentences.zh: 整曰：「本以張保肆逆，殺害無辜，闔州之人，俱陷不義。

translations.literal: Huzheng said, "Originally I acted because Zhang Bao rose in rebellion and slaughtered the innocent, plunging the whole prefecture into unrighteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Huzheng said, "I took arms because Zhang Bao rebelled and slaughtered innocents, drawing the whole prefecture into guilt.

sentences.zh: 今者同心，務在除凶，若共相推薦，復恐效尤致禍。

translations.literal: Now that we are of one mind, our task is to remove the criminal; if we recommend one another in turn, I fear we will invite imitation and bring disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Now we are united only to destroy the villain; if we begin recommending one another, others will imitate us and bring fresh calamity.

sentences.zh: 」於是乃波斯使主張道義行州事。

translations.literal: " He therefore had the Persian envoy Zhang Daoyi administer prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore placed Persian envoy Zhang Daoyi in charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 具以狀聞。

translations.literal: He reported the full circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: He reported everything to the court.

sentences.zh: 詔以申徽為刺史。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Shen Hui inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Shen Hui inspector.

sentences.zh: 徵整赴闕，授壽昌郡守，封襄武縣男。

translations.literal: Huzheng was summoned to court, appointed prefect of Shouchang commandery, and enfeoffed as Baron of Xiangwu county.
translations.idiomatic: Huzheng was recalled, made prefect of Shouchang, and enfeoffed as Baron of Xiangwu.

sentences.zh: 周文謂整曰：「卿早建殊勳，今官位未足酬賞，方當與卿共平天下，同取富貴。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou told Huzheng, "You early established outstanding merit; your present offices do not yet match your reward—I shall share with you the pacification of the realm and together we shall win wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen told him, "Your early deeds outrun your present rank. I mean to pacify the realm with you and share its rewards.

sentences.zh: 」遂立為瓜州義首。

translations.literal: " He was then established as leader of the loyal forces of Gua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " He was named head of the loyalist cause in Gua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 整以國難未甯，常願舉宗效力，遂率鄉親二千餘人入朝，隨軍征討。

translations.literal: Because the state's troubles were not yet settled, Huzheng constantly wished to bring his whole clan to serve; he therefore led more than two thousand fellow townsmen into court and followed the army on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: With the realm still unsettled, he led more than two thousand kinsmen and neighbors to court and marched with the armies.

sentences.zh: 整善於撫馭，躬同豐約，是以士眾並忘羈旅，盡其力用。

translations.literal: Huzheng was skilled in comforting and controlling troops; he shared their plenty and want in person, so the soldiers all forgot they were far from home and gave their utmost strength.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at leading men, he shared their hardships and comforts, so his followers forgot exile and fought with all their strength.

sentences.zh: 周文嘗從容謂整曰：「卿遠祖立忠而來，可謂積善余慶，世濟其美者也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen once said to Huzheng at leisure, "Your distant ancestor came west establishing loyalty—one may say accumulated goodness leaves surplus blessing, and generation after generation has carried on his excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once remarked to him, "Your distant ancestor came west in loyalty—truly accumulated virtue bears fruit, and your house has honored it ever since.

sentences.zh: 」整遠祖漢建威將軍邁，不為王莽屈，其子稱避地河右，故周文稱之云。

translations.literal: Huzheng's distant ancestor was the Han General Who Establishes Might Mai, who would not bow to Wang Mang; his son Cheng fled to the lands west of the Yellow River—therefore Emperor Wen spoke thus.
translations.idiomatic: That ancestor was Han General Who Establishes Might Mai, who refused Wang Mang; his son Cheng fled west of the Yellow River—hence the emperor's words.

sentences.zh: 累遷驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and General of the Upper Palace with the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies and made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General of Agile Cavalry and General of the Upper Palace with the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies and became Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 周文又謂整曰：「卿勳同婁、項，義等骨肉，立身敦雅，可以範人。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen again told Huzheng, "Your merit equals Lou and Xiang; your righteousness is like flesh and bone; your conduct is upright and cultured and can serve as a model for others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor added, "Your service rivals the great founders; your bond is kinship itself; your bearing is upright enough to teach a generation.

sentences.zh: 」遂賜姓宇文氏，並賜名整焉。

translations.literal: " He was therefore granted the surname Yuwen and also given the name Huzheng.
translations.idiomatic: " He was granted the imperial surname Yuwen and the personal name Huzheng.

sentences.zh: 宗人二百餘戶，並列屬籍。

translations.literal: More than two hundred households of his clan were all entered on the imperial register.
translations.idiomatic: More than two hundred households of his clan were enrolled in the imperial genealogy.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，拜司憲中大夫，處法平允，為當時所稱。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, he was appointed Grand Master of the Imperial Censorate; in applying the law he was fair and even, and was praised in his day.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he became Grand Master of the Imperial Censorate, applied the law with evenhanded fairness, and won contemporary praise.

sentences.zh: 進爵彭城縣公。

translations.literal: His enfeoffment was advanced to Duke of Pengcheng county.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Duke of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 初，梁興州刺史席固以州來附，周文以固為豐州刺史。

translations.literal: At first the Liang inspector of Xing Prefecture Xi Gu submitted his prefecture in allegiance; Emperor Wen made Gu inspector of Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Liang Inspector of Xing Prefecture Xi Gu had surrendered his prefecture; Emperor Wen made him inspector of Feng.

sentences.zh: 固蒞職既久，猶忌梁法，凡所施為，多虧政典。

translations.literal: Gu had long held office yet still clung to Liang law; in whatever he undertook he often violated the governing statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Long in office, Gu still clung to Liang practices and often violated Zhou statutes.

sentences.zh: 朝議密欲代之，而難其選。

translations.literal: Court discussion secretly wished to replace him but found the choice difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The court wished to replace him but could find no suitable man.

sentences.zh: 令整權鎮豐州，委以代固之略。

translations.literal: Huzheng was ordered to hold Feng Prefecture in temporary command and was entrusted with the plan to replace Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Huzheng was sent to hold Feng temporarily and entrusted with the plan to supplant Gu.

sentences.zh: 整廣布威恩，傾身撫接，數月之間，化洽州府。

translations.literal: Huzheng broadly spread authority and kindness and gave himself wholly to comforting the people; within a few months transformation pervaded the prefecture and offices.
translations.idiomatic: He spread kindness and authority alike and gave himself wholly to the people; within months the prefecture was transformed.

sentences.zh: 於是除整豐州刺史，以固為湖州。

translations.literal: Huzheng was then appointed inspector of Feng Prefecture and Gu was made inspector of Hu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huzheng was confirmed as inspector of Feng; Gu was moved to Hu.

sentences.zh: 豐州舊不居民中，賦役參集，勞逸不均。

translations.literal: Feng Prefecture had long had no fixed center among the people; taxes and corvée were heaped together and labor and rest were uneven.
translations.idiomatic: Feng had lacked a settled administrative center; taxes and labor fell unevenly on the people.

sentences.zh: 整請移居武當，詔可其奏。

translations.literal: Huzheng requested relocation to Wudang; an edict approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to move the seat to Wudang, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 獎勵撫導，遷者如歸，旬月之間，城府周備。

translations.literal: He encouraged, guided, and settled them, and those who moved came as if returning home; within a month the city walls and offices were complete.
translations.idiomatic: He guided the settlers with rewards and encouragement; within a month walls and offices stood complete.

sentences.zh: 固之遷也，其部曲多願留為整左右，整諭以朝制，弗之許焉，莫不流涕而去。

translations.literal: When Gu was transferred, many of his followers wished to remain at Huzheng's side; Huzheng explained the court's regulations and would not permit it, and they all left in tears.
translations.idiomatic: When Gu departed, many of his men wished to stay with Huzheng; he cited court law and refused, and they left weeping.

sentences.zh: 及整秩滿代至，人吏戀之，老幼送整，遠近畢集，數日停留，方得出界。

translations.literal: When Huzheng's term ended and his replacement arrived, officials and people were attached to him; old and young escorted Huzheng, gathering from far and near; for several days they lingered before he could cross the border.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, magistrates and people clung to him; young and old escorted him for days before he could leave the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其得人心如此。

translations.literal: Such was the way he won men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the hold he had on men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 拜禦正中大夫，出為中華郡守，轉同州司會，遷始州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Master of the Imperial Household, went out as prefect of Zhonghua commandery, was transferred to Director of the Bureau of Accounts of Tong Prefecture, and was promoted to inspector of Shi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became Grand Master of the Imperial Household, then prefect of Zhonghua, Director of Accounts for Tong Prefecture, and inspector of Shi.

sentences.zh: 整雅識情偽，尤明政術，恭謹廉慎，常懼盈滿，故曆居內外，所在見稱。

translations.literal: Huzheng finely discerned truth and falsehood and was especially clear in the arts of government; respectful, cautious, and frugal, he constantly feared excess, and therefore in every post at court and in the provinces he was praised wherever he served.
translations.idiomatic: Keen in reading men and masterful in administration, grave and frugal and ever wary of excess, he won praise in every office he held.

sentences.zh: 進位大將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to the rank of Great General.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Great General.

sentences.zh: 晉公護之初執政也，欲委整以腹心。

translations.literal: When Duke Yuwen Hu of Jin first took power he wished to entrust Huzheng with his innermost counsels.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Yuwen Hu first seized power he wished to make Huzheng his closest confidant.

sentences.zh: 整辭不敢當，頗忤其意，護以此疏之。

translations.literal: Huzheng declined and did not dare accept, which somewhat offended Hu's intent, and Hu therefore kept him at a distance for this.
translations.idiomatic: Huzheng declined, offending Hu, who thereafter kept his distance.

sentences.zh: 及護誅，附會者咸伏法，而整獨保全。

translations.literal: When Hu was executed, those who had attached themselves to him were all put to death by law, yet Huzheng alone was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu was executed, his partisans perished; Huzheng alone survived.

sentences.zh: 時人稱其先覺。

translations.literal: Men of the time praised his foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised his foresight.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，加四州諸軍事、鄜州刺史，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted his former offices, additionally made commander-in-chief of military affairs in four prefectures and inspector of Bin Prefecture, with the posthumous title Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted his former rank, made commander over four prefectures and inspector of Bin, with the posthumous title Xiang.

sentences.zh: 子熙嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xi inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 熙字長熙。

translations.literal: Xi, styled Changxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, whose style name was Changxi.

sentences.zh: 性嚴重，有雅量，雖在私室，終日儼然。

translations.literal: His nature was stern and weighty, with refined capacity; even in private quarters he remained grave all day.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and measured in temperament, he remained grave even in private.

sentences.zh: 不妄通賓客，凡所交結，必一時名士。

translations.literal: He did not casually receive guests; whoever he befriended had to be a leading figure of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He admitted no casual visitors; his friends were always men of note.

sentences.zh: 博覽群書，尤明三禮，善騎射，頗知音律。

translations.literal: He read widely in many books and was especially versed in the Three Rites; he was skilled in horsemanship and archery and quite knowledgeable in musical pitch.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely, excelled in the Three Rites, rode and shot well, and understood music.

sentences.zh: 起家以通經為吏部上士，轉夏官府都上士，俱有能名。

translations.literal: He first took office as Senior Clerk in the Ministry of Personnel through mastery of the classics, was transferred to Senior Clerk in the Bureau of Summer Offices of the Palace, and in both posts had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service through the classics as Senior Clerk in the Ministry of Personnel, then in the Palace Bureau of Summer Offices, distinguishing himself in both.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職，殆不勝喪。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning for his mother and nearly did not survive the grief.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning for his mother forced him from office; grief nearly destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 其父戒之曰：「大孝在於安親，義不絕嗣。

translations.literal: His father admonished him, "The greatest filial piety lies in bringing peace to one's parents; righteousness does not permit cutting off the line.
translations.idiomatic: His father warned him, "True filial piety comforts the living; righteousness forbids ending the line.

sentences.zh: 吾今見存，汝又只立，何得過爾毀頓，貽吾憂也？

translations.literal: I am still alive today, and you are my only son—how can you ruin yourself so utterly and hand me this worry?
translations.idiomatic: I am still alive, and you are my only heir—why destroy yourself and add to my grief?

sentences.zh: 」熙自是稍加饘粥。

translations.literal: " From then on Xi gradually took a little gruel.
translations.idiomatic: " After that he slowly took thin gruel.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除少駕部。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Junior Master of the Transport Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he became Junior Master of the Transport Bureau.

sentences.zh: 復丁父憂，非杖不起。

translations.literal: He again mourned his father and would not rise except leaning on a staff.
translations.idiomatic: At his father's death he would not rise without a staff.

sentences.zh: 人有聞其哭聲，莫不為之下泣。

translations.literal: Those who heard his weeping all wept for him in turn.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard him weep wept with him.

sentences.zh: 河陰之役，詔令墨衰從事，授職方下大夫，襲彭城縣公。

translations.literal: In the campaign at Heyin an edict ordered him to wear unhemmed mourning while serving; he was appointed Junior Master in the Bureau of Works and inherited the Dukedom of Pengcheng county.
translations.idiomatic: At Heyin the court ordered him to serve in unhemmed mourning; he became Junior Master in the Bureau of Works and inherited the dukedom of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 及武帝平齊，以留守功，進位儀同。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu pacified Qi, for his merit as defender he was advanced to the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu conquered Qi, his service as defender won him the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 曆司勳、吏部二曹中大夫，甚有當時譽。

translations.literal: He served successively as Grand Master in the Bureaus of Merits and of Personnel and had great reputation in his day.
translations.idiomatic: He held Grand Masterships in the Bureaus of Merits and Personnel in turn and enjoyed high repute.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪之際，熙以本官行納言事。

translations.literal: At the moment when Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, Xi acted in his original office as Master of Documents.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui accepted the throne, Xi served as acting Master of Documents.

sentences.zh: 尋除司徒左長史，加上儀同，進爵河南郡公。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Left Chief Clerk of the Secretariat, additionally granted Senior Ceremonial Regalia of the Three Excellencies, and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Henan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Left Chief Clerk of the Secretariat, received Senior Ceremonial Regalia of the Three Excellencies, and was raised to Duke of Henan.

sentences.zh: 時吐谷渾寇邊，以行軍長史從元帥元諧討之，以功進上開府。

translations.literal: At that time Tuyuhun raided the border; as campaigning chief clerk he followed the commander Yuan Xie in suppressing them and for merit was advanced to Senior General of the Upper Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuyuhun raided the frontier he followed Commander Yuan Xie as chief clerk, earned merit, and was made Senior General of the Upper Palace.

sentences.zh: 後拜滄州刺史，在職數年，風教大洽，稱為良二千石。

translations.literal: He was later appointed inspector of Cang Prefecture; during several years in office customs and teaching were greatly harmonized, and he was called a worthy administrator of two-thousand-bushel rank.
translations.idiomatic: As inspector of Cang for several years he transformed the region and was accounted a model prefect.

sentences.zh: 開皇四年，上幸洛陽。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaihuang the emperor visited Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaihuang the emperor traveled to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 熙來朝，吏人恐其遷，悲泣於道。

translations.literal: When Xi came to court, officials and people feared he would be transferred and wept along the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi came to court, magistrates and people feared transfer and wept in the streets.

sentences.zh: 及還，百姓出境迎謁，歡叫盈路。

translations.literal: When he returned, the common people went beyond the border to welcome and attend him, and shouts of joy filled the road.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the people went out beyond the border to welcome him, and cheers filled the road.

sentences.zh: 在州獲白烏、白麞、嘉麥，甘露降於庭前柳樹。

translations.literal: In the prefecture white crows, white musk deer, and fine wheat appeared, and sweet dew fell on the willow tree before the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: During his tenure white crows, white musk deer, and fine wheat appeared, and sweet dew fell on the courtyard willow.

sentences.zh: 八年，徙為河北道行台度支尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Minister of Revenue of the Hebei Circuit Executive.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became Minister of Revenue on the Hebei Circuit Executive.

sentences.zh: 吏人追思，相與立碑頌德。

translations.literal: Officials and people, recalling him with longing, together erected a stele praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates and people, missing him, raised a stele in his praise.

sentences.zh: 及行台廢，累遷鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: When the executive was abolished he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When the executive was abolished he rose to Grand Master of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 後以本官兼吏部尚書，往判五曹尚書事，民為明幹。

translations.literal: Later, in his original office additionally as Minister of Personnel, he went to decide the affairs of the Five Bureaus of Ministers; the people called him clear and capable.
translations.idiomatic: Later, additionally as Minister of Personnel, he adjudicated the Five Bureaus; the people called him sharp and effective.

sentences.zh: 上甚任之，用上祠太山，還次汴州，惡其殷盛，多有奸俠，以熙為汴州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly trusted him; when the emperor performed the suburban sacrifice at Mount Tai and on the return halted at Bian Prefecture, disliking its prosperity and the many scoundrels there, he made Xi inspector of Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor trusted him deeply. Returning from the Feng and Shan rites at Mount Tai, he stopped at Bian, disliked its bustle and rogues, and made Xi its inspector.

sentences.zh: 下車，禁遊食，抑工商，人有向術開門者杜之，船客停于郭外，星居者勒為聚落，僑人逐令歸本，其有滯獄，並決遣之，令行禁止。

translations.literal: On taking office he forbade wandering trades, restrained merchants and artisans, closed doors opened for divination, made traveling merchants halt outside the outer wall, compelled those living scattered to form settlements, ordered sojourners to return to their origins, and disposed of all pending cases—his orders were executed and his prohibitions observed.
translations.idiomatic: He banned street hawkers, curbed commerce, shut diviners' doors, kept travelers outside the walls, gathered scattered households into settlements, sent migrants home, and cleared every pending case—orders that were obeyed to the letter.

sentences.zh: 上聞而嘉之，顧侍臣曰：「鄴都，天下難臨處，敕相州刺史豆處通，令習熙法。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard he praised him and, turning to his attendants, said, "Ye is the hardest place in the realm to govern—I have instructed Xiangzhou Inspector Dou Chutong to study Xi's methods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him and told his attendants, "Ye is the hardest city in the empire to govern. I have ordered Xiangzhou Inspector Dou Chutong to learn Xi's methods.

sentences.zh: 」其年來朝，考績為天下之最。

translations.literal: " That year when he came to court his performance rating was the highest in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: " That year his performance review ranked first in the empire.

sentences.zh: 賜帛三百疋，頒告天下。

translations.literal: He was granted three hundred bolts of silk and the achievement was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He received three hundred bolts of silk, and the court proclaimed his achievement empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 以嶺南夷數起亂，徵拜桂州總管、十七州諸軍事，許以便宜從事，刺史已下官，得承制補授，給帳內五百人。

translations.literal: Because the southern barbarians repeatedly rose in rebellion, he was summoned and appointed commander-in-chief of Gui Prefecture and military affairs in seventeen prefectures, permitted to act as circumstances required; for officials from inspector downward he could appoint and confirm by imperial order, and he was given five hundred men within the commander's tent.
translations.idiomatic: When the southern tribes rebelled repeatedly, he was made commander-in-chief of Gui and military affairs across seventeen prefectures, with discretionary power to appoint officials through inspector rank and five hundred personal guards.

sentences.zh: 賜帛五百疋，發傳送其家累，改封武康郡公。

translations.literal: He was granted five hundred bolts of silk; an express relay transported his household; his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Wukang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He received five hundred bolts of silk, an express relay moved his household, and his title was changed to Duke of Wukang.

sentences.zh: 熙至部，大弘恩信。

translations.literal: When Xi reached his post he greatly spread favor and trust.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his command Xi extended favor and trust on a broad scale.

sentences.zh: 其溪洞渠帥更相謂曰：「前總管皆以兵威相脅，今者乃以手教相諭，我輩其可違乎！

translations.literal: The chieftains of the streams and caves said to one another, "Former commanders-in-chief all coerced us with military might; this one instructs us by personal letter—how can we disobey!
translations.idiomatic: The tribal chiefs said to one another, "Past commanders threatened us with arms; this one writes to us as to friends. How can we refuse?"

sentences.zh: 」於是相率歸附。

translations.literal: " They thereupon came forward in succession to submit.
translations.idiomatic: " They submitted one after another.

sentences.zh: 先是州縣生梗，長吏多不得之官，寄政于總管府。

translations.literal: Previously the prefectures and counties were unyielding, and the chief officials for the most part could not take their posts; administration was entrusted to the commander's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the region had been ungovernable and many prefects could not take office; affairs were run from the commander's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 熙悉遣之，為建城邑，開設學校，人夷感化焉。

translations.literal: Xi sent them all to their posts, built cities and towns for them, established schools, and both Chinese and barbarians were transformed by his influence.
translations.idiomatic: Xi sent officials to every post, built towns, opened schools, and won over both Chinese and tribes.

sentences.zh: 時有寧猛力者，與陳後主同日生，自言貌有貴相，在陳世已據南海。

translations.literal: At that time there was Ning Mengli, born on the same day as the Later Chen emperor, who claimed his features bore the marks of nobility; in Chen times he had already held Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: There was Ning Mengli, born the same day as the Chen emperor, who claimed a noble countenance and had held Nanhai under Chen.

sentences.zh: 平陳後，文帝因而撫之，即拜安州刺史。

translations.literal: After the pacification of Chen, Emperor Wen therefore comforted him and immediately appointed him inspector of An Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen fell, Emperor Wen conciliated him and made him inspector of An.

sentences.zh: 然驕倨恃險，未常參謁。

translations.literal: Yet he was arrogant and relied on difficult terrain, and never came to pay court.
translations.idiomatic: Proud and sheltered by difficult country, he never attended court.

sentences.zh: 熙手書諭之，申以交友之分。

translations.literal: Xi wrote to him in his own hand, appealing to the bond of friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Xi wrote personally, invoking their bond as friends.

sentences.zh: 其母有疾，熙復遺以藥。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill, Xi again sent her medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When Mengli's mother fell ill, Xi sent medicine.

sentences.zh: 猛力感之，詣府請謁，不敢為非。

translations.literal: Mengli was moved, came to the headquarters to request audience, and did not dare act wrongly.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, Mengli came to headquarters and dared no mischief.

sentences.zh: 熙以州縣多有同名，於是奏改安州為欽州，黃州為峰州，利州為智州，德州為歡州，東寧州為融州。

translations.literal: Because many prefectures and counties shared the same names, Xi memorialized to change An Prefecture to Qin Prefecture, Huang Prefecture to Feng Prefecture, Li Prefecture to Zhi Prefecture, De Prefecture to Huan Prefecture, and Dongning Prefecture to Rong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because many place names duplicated others, he memorialized to rename An as Qin, Huang as Feng, Li as Zhi, De as Huan, and Dongning as Rong.

sentences.zh: 上皆從之。

translations.literal: The emperor all approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all the changes.

sentences.zh: 在職數年，上表以年老疾患，請解所任。

translations.literal: After several years in office he submitted a memorial that, because of age and illness, he requested release from his duties.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he memorialized that age and illness obliged him to resign.

sentences.zh: 優詔不許，賜以醫藥。

translations.literal: A gracious edict did not permit it and granted him medicine.
translations.idiomatic: A gracious edict refused and sent him medicine.

sentences.zh: 熙奉詔令交州梁帥李佛子入朝，佛子欲為亂，請至仲冬上道。

translations.literal: Xi received the edict ordering Liang chieftain of Jiaozhou Li Fozi to enter court; Fozi wished to rebel and asked to set out only by mid-winter.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to bring Jiaozhou chieftain Li Fozi to court, Xi found Fozi plotting rebellion and asking delay until mid-winter.

sentences.zh: 熙意在羈縻，遂從之。

translations.literal: Xi's intent was to keep him on a loose rein, and he therefore agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Intending to keep him loosely tethered, Xi agreed.

sentences.zh: 有人詣闕，訟熙受佛子賂而舍之。

translations.literal: Someone went to the palace gate and accused Xi of accepting a bribe from Fozi and releasing him.
translations.idiomatic: Someone denounced Xi at court for taking Fozi's bribe and letting him go.

sentences.zh: 上聞。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard the charge.

sentences.zh: 佛子反問至，上大怒，以為信然，遣使鎖熙詣闕。

translations.literal: When word of Fozi's rebellion returned, the emperor was greatly enraged, believed it true, and sent an envoy to chain Xi and bring him to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Fozi rebelled, the emperor believed the accusation, flew into a rage, and sent men to chain Xi and bring him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 熙性素剛，鬱鬱不得志，行至永州，憂憤病卒。

translations.literal: Xi's nature had always been firm; depressed and unable to fulfill his aims, when he reached Yong Prefecture he died of grief and anger.
translations.idiomatic: Proud by nature and crushed by injustice, he fell ill with grief at Yong Prefecture and died.

sentences.zh: 上怒不解，沒其家財。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger did not subside, and his family's property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's wrath did not cool, and the family's property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 及行軍總管劉方禽佛子送京師，言熙實無贓。

translations.literal: When campaigning commander-in-chief Liu Fang captured Fozi and sent him to the capital, he said that Xi had truly taken no bribe.
translations.idiomatic: When Commander Liu Fang captured Fozi and sent him to the capital, he testified that Xi had taken no bribe.

sentences.zh: 上悟，乃召其四子聽仕。

translations.literal: The emperor understood, and then summoned his four sons to take office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and restored his four sons to office.

sentences.zh: 少子德棻最知名。

translations.literal: The youngest son Defen was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest son Defen became the most famous.

sentences.zh: 整弟休，幼聰敏，有文武材用。

translations.literal: Huzheng's younger brother Xiu was clever from childhood and had both civil and military talent.
translations.idiomatic: Huzheng's younger brother Xiu was clever as a boy and gifted in civil and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 與整同起兵逐張保，授帥都督。

translations.literal: He raised troops with Huzheng to drive out Zhang Bao and was appointed Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Huzheng in driving out Zhang Bao and was named Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 後為中外府樂曹參軍。

translations.literal: He later became Staff Officer in the Bureau of Music of the Inner and Outer Offices.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as staff officer in the Bureau of Music.

sentences.zh: 時諸功臣多為本州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time many meritorious ministers served as inspectors of their native prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Many great ministers then held their native prefectures.

sentences.zh: 晉公護謂整曰：「以公勳望，應得本州，但朝廷藉公委任，無容遠出。

translations.literal: Duke Yuwen Hu of Jin told Huzheng, "By your merit and standing you ought to receive your native prefecture, but the court relies on you for appointment and cannot allow you to go far.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Hu told Huzheng, "Your merit deserves your home prefecture, but the court cannot spare you.

sentences.zh: 然公一門之內，須有衣錦之榮。

translations.literal: Yet within your clan there must be the glory of returning home in brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Still, your house should have one man who returns in glory.

sentences.zh: 」乃以休為敦煌郡守。

translations.literal: " He therefore made Xiu prefect of Dunhuang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " He made Xiu prefect of Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 在郡十餘年，甚有政績。

translations.literal: During more than ten years in the commandery he had great administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years he governed Dunhuang with distinction.

sentences.zh: 卒于合州刺史。

translations.literal: He died as inspector of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as inspector of He Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 唐永，北海平壽人也。

translations.literal: Tang Yong was a native of Pingshou in Beihai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yong came from Pingshou in Beihai commandery.

sentences.zh: 本居晉昌之憤安縣，晉亂，徙于丹楊。

translations.literal: His family originally lived in Fen'an county of Jinchang; during the Jin turmoil they moved to Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: His family had lived in Fen'an in Jinchang; during the Jin disorders they moved to Danyang.

sentences.zh: 祖揣，始遠魏，官至北海太守，因家焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chuai first went far to Wei, reached the post of prefect of Beihai commandery, and settled his family there.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chuai first entered Wei, became prefect of Beihai, and settled there.

sentences.zh: 父倫，青州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Lun was inspector of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lun was inspector of Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 永身長八尺，少耿介，有將帥才，讀《班超傳》，慨然有萬里之志。

translations.literal: Yong was eight feet tall; from youth he was high-minded and had the talent of a general; reading the biography of Ban Chao, he was stirred with the ambition to travel ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Eight feet tall, high-spirited from youth, and gifted as a commander, he read Ban Chao's biography and burned with ambition to win fame far from home.

sentences.zh: 正光中，為北地太守，當郡別將。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguang era he was prefect of Beidi commandery and separate commander of that commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguang era he was prefect of Beidi and its separate commander.

sentences.zh: 俄而賊將宿勤明達、車金雀等寇郡境，永擊破之，境內稍安。

translations.literal: Before long the bandit generals Su Qinmingda and Che Jinque and others raided the commandery borders; Yong defeated them and the territory was gradually pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Soon bandit generals Su Qinmingda and Che Jinque raided the borders; Yong defeated them and restored peace.

sentences.zh: 永善馭下，士人競為之用。

translations.literal: Yong was skilled in controlling subordinates, and gentlemen and commoners alike competed to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at leading men, gentry and commoners alike flocked to his banner.

sentences.zh: 熙陣常著帛裙襦，把角如意以指麾處分，辭色自若。

translations.literal: In battle Yong always wore a silk skirt-robe, held a horn ruyi scepter to command and dispose, and his words and bearing were calm.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he wore a silk robe, directed troops with a horn ruyi scepter in hand, and never lost his composure.

sentences.zh: 在北地四年，與賊數十戰，未常敗北。

translations.literal: In Beidi for four years he fought the bandits in several dozen battles and never suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: For four years in Beidi he fought dozens of engagements and never lost.

sentences.zh: 時人語曰：「莫陸梁，恐爾逢唐將。

translations.literal: Men of the time said, "Do not make trouble—you may meet the Tang general.
translations.idiomatic: People said, "Make no trouble, lest you meet General Tang.

sentences.zh: 」永所營處，至今猶稱唐公壘也。

translations.literal: " The camps Yong built are still called Duke Tang's ramparts today.
translations.idiomatic: " His camps are still called Duke Tang's ramparts.

sentences.zh: 行台蕭寶夤表永為南幽州刺史，夷人送故者，莫不垂淚，當路遮留，隨數日，始得出境。

translations.literal: The Commissioner-in-Chief Xiao Baoyin memorialized Yong as inspector of Southern You Prefecture; the barbarians who escorted him on his departure all wept; those on the road blocked and detained him, and only after several days could he leave the border.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Xiao Baoyin recommended him as inspector of Southern You; tribesmen who escorted him wept, and travelers blocked his path for days before he could cross the border.

sentences.zh: 大統元年，拜東雍州刺史，尋加衛將軍，封平壽伯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong he was appointed inspector of Eastern Yong Prefecture and soon additionally made Guard General and enfeoffed as Earl of Pingshou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong he became inspector of Eastern Yong, then Guard General and Earl of Pingshou.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空公。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Duke of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Duke of Works.

sentences.zh: 永性清廉，家無蓄積，妻子不免饑寒，世以此稱之。

translations.literal: Yong's nature was pure and incorrupt; his house had no stores, and his wife and children did not escape hunger and cold—the age praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Pure and incorruptible, he left no stores; his wife and children knew hunger and cold, and the age praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 子陵，少習武藝，頗閑吏職，位大都督、應州刺史、車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: His son Ling from youth practiced martial arts, was quite versed in official duties, and reached the posts of Grand Commander, inspector of Ying Prefecture, General of the Chariots and Cavalry, and the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ling trained in arms from youth, mastered official routine, and rose to Grand Commander, inspector of Ying, General of the Chariots and Cavalry, and the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 陵子悟，美風儀，博涉經史，文詠可觀。

translations.literal: Ling's son Wu had fine bearing, read widely in the classics and histories, and his literary compositions were admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Ling's son Wu was handsome, widely read, and wrote admirable verse.

sentences.zh: 周大象中，頗被宣帝任遇，位至內史下大夫、漢陽公。

translations.literal: In the Daxiang era of Zhou he was greatly favored by Emperor Xuan and reached the post of Junior Master in the Secretariat and Duke of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan in the Daxiang era he won high favor and became Junior Master in the Secretariat and Duke of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝得政，廢於家而卒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui seized power he was dismissed to his home and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took power he was dismissed and died at home.

sentences.zh: 陵弟瑾。

translations.literal: Ling's younger brother Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Ling's younger brother Jin is also treated here.

sentences.zh: 瑾字附璘。

translations.literal: Jin, styled Fulian.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, whose style name was Fulian.

sentences.zh: 性溫恭，有器量，博涉經史，雅好屬文。

translations.literal: His nature was mild and respectful, with capacity; he read widely in the classics and histories and was by nature fond of composing literature.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle, measured, and widely learned, he loved literary composition.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺二寸，容貌甚偉。

translations.literal: He was eight feet two inches tall, and his appearance was very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: Eight feet two inches tall, he was imposing in appearance.

sentences.zh: 年十七，周文聞其名，乃貽永書曰：「聞公有二子，曰陵、曰瑾，陵從橫多武略，瑾雍容富文雅，可並遣入朝，孤欲委以文武之任。

translations.literal: At seventeen Emperor Wen of Zhou heard his name and therefore sent Yong a letter saying, "I hear you have two sons, named Ling and Jin; Ling is versatile and full of military stratagems, Jin is dignified and rich in literary elegance—they may both be sent to court; I wish to entrust them with civil and military duties.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen Jin's fame reached Emperor Wen of Zhou, who wrote to Yong, "I hear your sons Ling and Jin excel—the one in arms, the other in letters. Send them to court; I will use them in civil and military posts.

sentences.zh: 」因召拜尚書員外郎、相府記室參軍事。

translations.literal: " He was therefore summoned and appointed Supernumerary Gentleman in the Secretariat and Staff Officer in the Chancellor's Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: " He was summoned, made Supernumerary Gentleman in the Secretariat, and staff officer in the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 軍書羽檄，瑾多掌之。

translations.literal: Military documents and urgent dispatches were largely handled by Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He handled most military documents and urgent dispatches.

sentences.zh: 從破沙苑，戰河橋，並有功，封姑藏縣子。

translations.literal: He followed in breaking Shaoyuan, fought at Heqiao, and all had battle merit; he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Guniang county.
