translations.idiomatic: He shared in the victory at Shaoyuan and fought at Heqiao, earning enfeoffment as Viscount of Guniang.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書右丞、吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Right Assistant in the Secretariat and Gentleman in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Right Assistant in the Secretariat and Gentleman in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 于時魏室播遷，庶務草創，朝章國典，瑾並參之。

translations.literal: At that time the Wei court was driven to wander and every task was newly founded; court regulations and state statutes—Jin participated in all of them.
translations.idiomatic: With the Wei court in exile and institutions being built anew, he helped shape court law and state statutes.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部尚書，進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Household Revenue, advanced to General of Agile Cavalry and General of the Upper Palace with the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies, and granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: He became Minister of the Household Revenue, General of Agile Cavalry and General of the Upper Palace with the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies, and received the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 時燕公於謹，勳高望重，朝野所屬。

translations.literal: At that time Duke Yuwen Jin of Yan had high merit and great standing and was the hope of court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Yuwen Jin of Yan then stood at the pinnacle of merit and public esteem.

sentences.zh: 白周文，言瑾學行兼修，願與之同姓，結為兄弟，庶子孫承其餘論，有益義方。

translations.literal: He informed Emperor Wen that Jin's learning and conduct were both cultivated and that he wished to share the same surname and become sworn brothers, so that posterity might inherit his remaining teachings and benefit moral instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He told Emperor Wen that Jin's learning and conduct were exemplary, asked to share his surname and become sworn brothers, so posterity might inherit his teaching.

sentences.zh: 周文歎異者久之，更賜瑾姓萬紐於氏。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen marveled at this for a long time and again granted Jin the surname Wanniu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled and granted Jin the surname Wanniu.

sentences.zh: 謹乃深相結納，敦長幼之序；

translations.literal: Jin thereupon formed a deep bond with him and honored the order of elder and younger;
translations.idiomatic: Jin formed a deep bond with him and honored the order of elder and younger;

sentences.zh: 瑾亦庭羅子孫，行弟侄之敬。

translations.literal: Jin also arrayed his sons and grandsons in the hall and showed the respect due between younger brother and nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Jin arrayed his sons and grandsons in the hall and showed them the respect due between junior kin.

sentences.zh: 其為朝望所宗如此。

translations.literal: Such was the way he was honored by court expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which the court held him.

sentences.zh: 進爵臨淄縣伯。

translations.literal: His enfeoffment was advanced to Earl of Linzi county.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Earl of Linzi.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部尚書，銓綜衡流，雅有人倫之鑒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel and in weighing and selecting the current of talent had a refined eye for human relations.
translations.idiomatic: As Minister of Personnel he weighed candidates with a refined eye for character.

sentences.zh: 以父憂去職，尋起令視事。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning for his father and soon was ordered to resume and oversee affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father but was soon ordered back to duty.

sentences.zh: 時六尚書皆一時之秀，周文自謂得人，號為六俊，然瑾尤見器重。

translations.literal: At that time the six ministers were all outstanding men of the age; Emperor Wen of Zhou himself said he had obtained the right men and called them the Six Talents, yet Jin was especially trusted.
translations.idiomatic: All six ministers were outstanding; the emperor called them the Six Talents, yet trusted Jin above the rest.

sentences.zh: 于謹南伐江陵，以瑾為元帥府長史，軍中謀略，多出瑾焉。

translations.literal: When Yu Jin campaigned south against Jiangling, Jin was made chief clerk of the commander's headquarters, and military stratagems largely came from Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Jin marched on Jiangling, Jin served as chief clerk and shaped most of the strategy.

sentences.zh: 江陵既平，衣冠仕伍，並沒為僕隸。

translations.literal: After Jiangling was pacified, gentry and soldiers alike were all taken as slaves.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangling fell, gentry and soldiers alike were enslaved.

sentences.zh: 瑾察其才行有片善者，輒議免之，賴瑾獲濟者甚眾。

translations.literal: Wherever Jin discerned in their conduct and ability even a shred of good, he at once proposed their release; those who escaped ruin thanks to Jin were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he found even a trace of merit he proposed release; multitudes owed him their freedom.

sentences.zh: 時論多焉。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 及軍還，諸將多因虜掠，大獲財物。

translations.literal: When the army returned, many generals because of captive plunder obtained great wealth.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march many generals grew rich from plunder.

sentences.zh: 瑾一無所取，唯得書兩車，載之以歸。

translations.literal: Jin took nothing at all, obtaining only two cartloads of books, which he carried home.
translations.idiomatic: Jin took nothing but two cartloads of books.

sentences.zh: 或白周文曰：「唐瑾大有輜重，悉是梁朝珍玩。

translations.literal: Someone informed Emperor Wen, "Tang Jin has great baggage, all precious objects of the Liang court.
translations.idiomatic: Someone told the emperor, "Tang Jin's wagons are full of Liang treasures.

sentences.zh: 」周文初不信之，然欲明其虛實，密遣使檢閱之，唯見墳籍而已。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wen at first did not believe it, yet wished to clarify the truth and falsehood and secretly sent an envoy to inspect; he saw only books and records.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor doubted it but sent a secret inspection and found only books.

sentences.zh: 乃歎曰：「孤知此人來二十許年，明其不以利幹義。

translations.literal: He then sighed and said, "I have known this man for some twenty years and understood that he would not let profit move his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and said, "I have known this man twenty years and knew he would not trade righteousness for gain.

sentences.zh: 向若不令檢視，恐常人有投杼之疑。

translations.literal: If I had not ordered inspection, I feared ordinary men would have the suspicion of casting away the pestle.
translations.idiomatic: Without inspection, ordinary men might have suspected him like the mother who cast away her pestle.

sentences.zh: 孤所以益明之耳。

translations.literal: I have only made this clearer.
translations.idiomatic: I have only made his integrity clearer.

sentences.zh: 凡受人委任當如此也。

translations.literal: All who accept another's commission ought to be like this.
translations.idiomatic: All who accept office should be like this.

sentences.zh: 」論平江陵功，進爵為公。

translations.literal: " In assessing merit for pacifying Jiangling, his enfeoffment was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: " For the pacification of Jiangling he was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 六官建，授禮部中大夫。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established he was appointed Grand Master of the Bureau of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were created he became Grand Master of the Bureau of Rites.

sentences.zh: 出為蔡州刺史，曆拓州、硤州，所在皆有德化，人吏稱之。

translations.literal: He went out as inspector of Cai Prefecture and served successively in Tuo and Xia prefectures; wherever he was there was virtuous transformation, and officials and people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: As inspector of Cai and then Tuo and Xia he won praise wherever he governed.

sentences.zh: 轉荊州總管府長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief clerk of the Jing Prefecture commander's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He became chief clerk at Jing Prefecture headquarters.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部中大夫，曆禦正、納言、內史中大夫。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Grand Master in the Ministry of Personnel and served successively as Grand Master of the Imperial Household, Master of Documents, and Grand Master in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Grand Master in the Ministry of Personnel and held in turn the posts of Grand Master of the Imperial Household, Master of Documents, and Grand Master in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 曾未十旬，遂遷四職，搢紳咸以為榮。

translations.literal: In less than ten ten-day periods he was transferred through four posts, and gentry and officials all regarded it as glory.
translations.idiomatic: In less than a hundred days he passed through four offices, to the envy of the court.

sentences.zh: 久之，除司宗中大夫，兼內史。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed Grand Master of the Imperial Clan and additionally Master of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Grand Master of the Imperial Clan and additionally Master of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於位。

translations.literal: He soon died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈小宗伯，諡曰方。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Minister of the Imperial Clan with the posthumous title Fang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Minister of the Imperial Clan with the posthumous title Fang.

sentences.zh: 瑾性方重，有風格，退朝休假，恆著衣冠以對妻子，遇迅雷風烈，雖閑夜晏寢，必起，冠帶端笏危坐。

translations.literal: Jin's nature was square and weighty, with bearing; when he left court on holiday he always wore cap and robes before his wife and children, and when thunder and violent wind came, even in the quiet of night in bed he would rise, put on cap and belt, straighten his tablet, and sit in formal posture.
translations.idiomatic: Square and dignified in character, he wore formal dress even before his family on holidays, and at thunder or gale—even deep in the night—he would rise, robe himself, straighten his tablet, and sit formally.

sentences.zh: 又好施與，家無餘財，所得祿賜，常散之宗族，其尤貧乏者，又割膏腴田宅以振之。

translations.literal: He was also fond of giving; his house had no surplus wealth; the salary and gifts he received he constantly distributed among his clan, and for those in extreme poverty he also cut off fertile fields and residences to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: Generous by nature, he kept no surplus; he gave salary and gifts to his clan, and carved fertile lands from his estate for the poorest.

sentences.zh: 所留遺子孫者，並墝埆之地。

translations.literal: What he left to sons and grandsons was all poor and stony land.
translations.idiomatic: What he left his descendants was stony, unproductive soil.

sentences.zh: 朝野以此稱之。

translations.literal: Court and countryside praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside alike praised him.

sentences.zh: 撰《新儀》十篇，所著賦、頌、碑、誄二十餘萬言。

translations.literal: He compiled ten chapters of New Rites and composed more than two hundred thousand characters of fu, eulogies, stele inscriptions, and dirges.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote ten chapters of New Rites and more than two hundred thousand characters of fu, eulogies, steles, and dirges.

sentences.zh: 孫大智嗣。

translations.literal: His grandson Dazhi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Dazhi inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 瑾次子令則，性好篇章，兼解音律，文多輕豔，為時人所傳。

translations.literal: Jin's second son Lingze loved literary composition and also understood musical pitch; his writings were often light and ornate and were transmitted among men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's second son Lingze loved verse and understood music; his often ornate writings circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 天和初，以齊馭下大夫使于陳。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianhe, as Junior Master of the Chariots and Cavalry of Qi he was envoy to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianhe he went to Chen as Junior Master of the Chariots and Cavalry of Qi.

sentences.zh: 大象中，官至樂部下大夫。

translations.literal: In the Daxiang era he reached the post of Junior Master in the Bureau of Music.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daxiang era he became Junior Master in the Bureau of Music.

sentences.zh: 仕隋，位太子左庶子。

translations.literal: Serving Sui, he held the post of Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui he was Left Assistant to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 皇太子勇廢，被誅。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Yong was deposed, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Yong was deposed, he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 柳敏，字白澤，河東解縣人，晉太常純之七世孫也。

translations.literal: Liu Min, styled Baize, was a native of Jie county in Hedong commandery, a seventh-generation descendant of Chun, Jin Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Min, whose style name was Baize, came from Jie in Hedong, seventh in descent from Jin Grand Master of Ceremonies Chun.

sentences.zh: 父懿，魏車騎大將軍、儀同三司、汾州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yi was Wei General of the Chariots and Cavalry, held the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies, and was inspector of Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi was Wei General of the Chariots and Cavalry with the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies and inspector of Fen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 敏九歲而孤，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Min was orphaned at nine and served his mother with a reputation for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at nine, he won fame for filial service to his mother.

sentences.zh: 性好學，涉獵經史，陰陽卜筮之術，靡不習焉。

translations.literal: His nature loved learning; he ranged through the classics and histories and the arts of yin-yang divination and milfoil—there was none he did not study.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning, ranged through classics and histories, and mastered yin-yang divination and milfoil.

sentences.zh: 年未弱冠，起家員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Before he had reached the capping age he first took office as Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Before his capping ceremony he entered service as Supernumerary Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 累遷河東郡丞。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Assistant in Hedong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to assistant prefect of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 朝議以敏之本邑，故有此授。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that because it was Min's native commandery, he received this appointment for that reason.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave him his home commandery for that reason.

sentences.zh: 敏雖統御鄉里，而處物平允，甚得時譽。

translations.literal: Though Min governed his native district, in dealing with affairs he was fair and even and won great reputation in his day.
translations.idiomatic: Though governing his home district, he was evenhanded and widely praised.

sentences.zh: 及周文克復河東，見而器異之，乃謂之曰：「今日不喜得河東，喜得卿也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou recovered Hedong and saw him, he was struck by his talent and told him, "Today I am not glad to have gained Hedong—I am glad to have gained you.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen recovered Hedong and met him, he said, "Today I rejoice not in Hedong but in winning you.

sentences.zh: 」即拜丞相府參軍事。

translations.literal: " He was immediately appointed staff officer in the Chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: " He was at once made staff officer in the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 俄轉戶曹參軍，兼記室。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to staff officer in the Bureau of the Household and additionally Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was staff officer in the Bureau of the Household and additionally recorder.

sentences.zh: 每有四方賓客，恆令接之，爰及吉凶禮儀，亦令監綜。

translations.literal: Whenever there were guests from the four directions he was always ordered to receive them, and in auspicious and inauspicious rites and ceremonies he was also ordered to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: He received guests from all quarters and oversaw ritual observances.

sentences.zh: 又與蘇綽等修撰新制，為朝廷政典。

translations.literal: He also joined Su Chuo and others in compiling new regulations as the governing statutes of the court.
translations.idiomatic: With Su Chuo and others he helped draft the new regulations that became the court's governing code.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部郎中，封武城縣子，加帥都督，領本鄉兵。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman in the Bureau of Rites, enfeoffed as Viscount of Wucheng county, additionally made Commander-in-Chief, and placed in command of the militia of his native township.
translations.idiomatic: He became Gentleman in the Bureau of Rites, Viscount of Wucheng, Commander-in-Chief, and head of his home militia.

sentences.zh: 俄進大都督。

translations.literal: Shortly he was advanced to Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，居喪，旬日之間，鬢髮半白。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother; in mourning, within ten days half his hair turned white.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning his mother, half his hair turned white within ten days.

sentences.zh: 尋起為吏部郎中，毀瘠過禮，杖而後起。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as Gentleman in the Ministry of Personnel; his emaciation from grief exceeded the rites, and he rose only with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Gentleman in the Ministry of Personnel, he was so wasted by grief that he needed a staff to rise.

sentences.zh: 周文見而歎異之，特加稟賜。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou saw this and marveled, granting him special gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen marveled and granted him special gifts.

sentences.zh: 及尉遲迥伐蜀，以敏為行軍司馬，軍中籌略，並以委之。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Jiong campaigned against Shu, Min was made campaigning chief clerk, and military stratagems were all entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong marched on Shu, Min served as chief clerk and directed the strategy.

sentences.zh: 益州平，進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中，遷尚書，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: When Yi Prefecture was pacified he was advanced to General of Agile Cavalry and General of the Upper Palace with the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies, made Palace Attendant, transferred to the Secretariat, and granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu was pacified he became General of Agile Cavalry and General of the Upper Palace with the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies, Palace Attendant, and Minister of the Secretariat, and received the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜禮部中大夫。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established he was appointed Grand Master of the Bureau of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were created he became Grand Master of the Bureau of Rites.

sentences.zh: 昂字千里。

translations.literal: Ang, styled Qianli.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ang, whose style name was Qianli.

sentences.zh: 幼聰穎有器識，幹局過人。

translations.literal: From childhood he was clever and keen with judgment; his capacity for affairs surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and far-seeing from boyhood, his executive talent surpassed other men's.

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，為內史中大夫、開府儀同三司，賜爵文城郡公，當途用事，百僚皆出其下。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou he was Grand Master in the Secretariat and General of the Upper Palace with the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies, enfeoffed as Duke of Wencheng commandery; holding power on the road, the hundred officials were all beneath him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Zhou he was Grand Master in the Secretariat and General of the Upper Palace with the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies and Duke of Wencheng, dominating the court so that every official stood beneath him.

sentences.zh: 昂竭誠獻替，知無不為，謙虛自處，未嘗驕物，時論以此重之。

translations.literal: Ang devoted himself in loyal remonstrance, knowing nothing he would not undertake; humble in his bearing, he never showed arrogance toward others, and contemporary opinion for this honored him.
translations.idiomatic: He remonstrated loyally on every matter, remained humble and never arrogant, and the age respected him for it.

sentences.zh: 武帝崩，受遺輔政，稍被宣帝疏，然不離本職。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu died he received the testamentary charge to assist in government and was gradually kept at a distance by Emperor Xuan, yet he did not leave his original post.
translations.idiomatic: Named regent at Emperor Wu's death, he was gradually distanced by Emperor Xuan but never left office.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為丞相，深自結納。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was Chancellor he formed a deep bond with Ang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chancellor he drew Ang into a close bond.

sentences.zh: 文帝以為大宗伯。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen made him Grand Minister of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named him Grand Minister of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 拜日，遂得偏風，不能視事。

translations.literal: On the day of his appointment he suffered hemiplegia and could not conduct affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of appointment he suffered a stroke and could not govern.

sentences.zh: 文帝受禪，疾愈，加上開府，拜潞州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen received the abdication his illness improved; he was additionally granted Senior General of the Upper Palace and appointed inspector of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne Ang recovered, was made Senior General of the Upper Palace, and became inspector of Lu.

sentences.zh: 昂見天下無事，上表請勸學行禮。

translations.literal: Ang saw that the realm was at peace and submitted a memorial requesting encouragement of learning and practice of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the realm at peace, he memorialized to promote learning and ritual.

sentences.zh: 上覽而善之，優詔答昂，自是天下州縣皆置博士習禮焉。

translations.literal: The emperor read it and approved; a gracious edict replied to Ang, and from then on every prefecture and county in the realm appointed erudites to study ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and replied graciously; thereafter every prefecture and county appointed erudites to teach ritual.

sentences.zh: 昂在州，甚有惠政，卒官。

translations.literal: Ang in the prefecture had very benevolent administration and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Lu with great benevolence and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子調，曆秘書郎、侍御史。

translations.literal: His son Diao served successively as Secretary Gentleman and Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Diao served as Secretary Gentleman and Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 左僕射楊素嘗於朝堂見調，因獨言日：「柳條通體弱，獨搖不須風」調斂版正色曰：「調信無取，公不當以為侍御；

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Yang Su once saw Diao in the court hall and therefore said alone by day, "Willow branches are weak throughout, swaying without need of wind." Diao straightened his tablet and said with a stern face, "If Diao truly has nothing to offer, you ought not make him Attending Censor;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yang Su once saw Diao in court and remarked aloud, "Willow branches are weak all through—they sway without wind." Diao straightened his tablet and said sternly, "If I am worthless, you should not have made me censor;

sentences.zh: 信有可取，不應發此言。

translations.literal: if he truly has something to offer, you ought not to speak such words.
translations.idiomatic: if I have merit, you should not speak so.

sentences.zh: 公當具瞻之地，樞機何可輕發！

translations.literal: You stand in a place where all eyes are fixed; how can the pivot of state lightly speak thus!
translations.idiomatic: You stand where all eyes are fixed—how can the pivot of state speak so lightly!

sentences.zh: 」素甚奇之。

translations.literal: " Su greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: " Su marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，累遷尚書左司郎中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Diao was repeatedly promoted to Left Bureau Chief in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang he rose to Left Bureau Chief in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時王綱不振，朝士多贓貨，唯調清素守常，為時所美，然幹用非其所長。

translations.literal: At that time the royal norms were slack and court gentlemen mostly took bribes; only Diao was pure and upheld constancy, and was praised in his day, yet practical executive talent was not his strong point.
translations.idiomatic: With court discipline slack and officials corrupt, only Diao remained pure and was praised, though executive talent was not his strength.

sentences.zh: 王士良，字君明，其先太原晉陽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Shiliang, styled Junming, had ancestors who were natives of Jinyang in Taiyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shiliang, whose style name was Junming, traced his line to Jinyang in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 後因晉亂，避地涼州。

translations.literal: Later because of the Jin turmoil they took refuge in Liang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jin disorders the family fled to Liang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 魏太武平沮渠氏，曾祖景仁歸魏，為敦煌鎮將。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu of Wei pacified the Juqu clan, his great-grandfather Jingren submitted to Wei and became garrison general of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu of Wei conquered the Juqu, his great-grandfather Jingren submitted and became Dunhuang garrison general.

sentences.zh: 祖公禮，平城鎮司馬，因家於代。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gongli was Military Administrator of Pingcheng and settled his family in Dai.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gongli was Military Administrator of Pingcheng and settled the family in Dai.

sentences.zh: 父延，蘭陵郡守。

translations.literal: His father Yan was prefect of Lanling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan was prefect of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 士良少修謹，不妄交遊。

translations.literal: From youth Shiliang cultivated prudence and did not casually form friendships.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was careful and formed no casual friendships.

sentences.zh: 孝莊末，爾硃仲遠啟為府參軍事。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xiaozhuang era Erzhu Zhongyuan recommended him as staff officer in his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign Erzhu Zhongyuan took him on as staff officer.

sentences.zh: 曆大行台郎中、諫議大夫，封石門縣男。

translations.literal: He served successively as Gentleman in the Grand Commissioner-in-Chief's office and Remonstrating and Consulting Grand Master, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Shimen county.
translations.idiomatic: He served as gentleman in the grand commissioner's office and remonstrating grand master, and was enfeoffed Baron of Shimen.

sentences.zh: 後與紇豆陵步籓交戰，軍敗，為籓所禽，遂居河右。

translations.literal: Later he fought with Qidouling Bubu and was defeated; he was taken by Bubu and therefore lived west of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Later, defeated and captured by Qidouling Bubu in battle, he remained west of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 偽行台紇豆陵伊利欽其才，擢授右丞，妻以孫女。

translations.literal: The false Commissioner-in-Chief Qidouling Yili admired his talent, promoted him to Right Assistant, and gave him his granddaughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel commissioner Qidouling Yili admired his talent, made him Right Assistant, and gave him his granddaughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 士良既為姻好，便得盡言，遂曉以禍福，伊利等即歸附。

translations.literal: Shiliang, now linked by marriage, was able to speak freely; he thereupon enlightened them with fortune and calamity, and Yili and the others at once submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Through the marriage alliance he spoke freely, showed them fortune and ruin, and Yili and his followers submitted.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之。

translations.literal: The court praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended him.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，進爵晉陽縣子，尋進爵琅邪縣侯，授太中大夫、右將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang his enfeoffment was advanced to Viscount of Jinyang county; soon it was advanced to Marquis of Langye county; he was appointed Grand Master of Palace Counsel and General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taichang he was raised to Viscount of Jinyang, then Marquis of Langye, Grand Master of Palace Counsel, and General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 出為殷州車騎府司馬。

translations.literal: He went out as Military Administrator of the Chariots and Cavalry Bureau of Yin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became Military Administrator of the Chariots and Cavalry Bureau of Yin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 東魏徙鄴之後，置京畿府，專典兵馬。

translations.literal: After Eastern Wei moved the capital to Ye, the Capital Region headquarters was established to specialize in troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: After Eastern Wei moved to Ye, a Capital Region headquarters was created to manage troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 時齊文襄為大都督，以士良為司馬，領外兵參軍。

translations.literal: At that time Duke Wenxiang of Qi was Grand Commander and made Shiliang his chief of staff, additionally placing him in charge of external military affairs as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wenxiang of Qi, then Grand Commander, made him chief of staff and staff officer in charge of external military affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋遷長史，加安西將軍，徙封符壘縣侯。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Chief Clerk, additionally made General Who Pacifies the West, and his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Fulei county.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became chief clerk and General Who Pacifies the West and was re-enfeoffed Marquis of Fulei.

sentences.zh: 武定初，除行台右中兵郎中，又轉大將軍府屬、從事中郎，仍攝外兵事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuding he was appointed Right Central Military Gentleman in the Commissioner-in-Chief's office, then transferred to staff in the Grand General's headquarters and Attendant Gentleman, still overseeing external military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wuding he was Right Central Military Gentleman in the commissioner's office, then staff in the grand general's headquarters and Attendant Gentleman, still overseeing external military affairs.

sentences.zh: 王思政鎮穎川，齊文襄率眾攻之。

translations.literal: Wang Sizheng held Yingchuan; Duke Wenxiang of Qi led the masses to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng held Yingchuan; Duke Wenxiang besieged him.

sentences.zh: 授士良大行台左丞，加鎮西將軍，進爵為公，令輔其弟演于并州居守。

translations.literal: Shiliang was appointed Left Assistant in the Grand Commissioner-in-Chief's office, additionally made General Who Pacifies the West, advanced in enfeoffment to duke, and ordered to assist his younger brother Yan in holding Bing Prefecture in defense.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Left Assistant in the grand commissioner's office, General Who Pacifies the West, and duke, and ordered to assist his younger brother Yan in defending Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 齊文宣即位，入為給事黃門侍郎，領中書舍人，仍總知并州兵馬事，加征西將軍，別封新豐縣子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenxuan of Qi took the throne he entered court as Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Supervisor of the Secretariat, still in overall charge of Bing Prefecture military affairs, additionally made General Who Pacifies the West, and separately enfeoffed as Viscount of Xinfeng county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenxuan ascended the throne he became Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Supervisor of the Secretariat, still commanding Bing military affairs, with additional rank as General Who Pacifies the West and separate enfeoffment as Viscount of Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 俄除驃騎將軍、尚書吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry and Gentleman in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was General of Agile Cavalry and Gentleman in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 文宣自晉陽赴鄴宮，復以士良為尚書左丞，統留後事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenxuan went from Jinyang to the Ye palace, he again made Shiliang Left Assistant in the Secretariat to oversee affairs left behind.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxuan went from Jinyang to Ye, he again made Shiliang Left Assistant in the Secretariat to oversee affairs in the capital.

sentences.zh: 仍遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He then became Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 轉七兵尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Seven Armies.
translations.idiomatic: He became Minister of the Seven Armies.

sentences.zh: 未幾，入為侍中，轉殿中尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he entered court as Palace Attendant and was transferred to Minister of the Palace Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was Palace Attendant, then Minister of the Palace Bureau.

sentences.zh: 頃之，復為侍中、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly he again served as Palace Attendant and Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he again held Palace Attendant and Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 士良少孤，事繼母梁氏以孝聞。

translations.literal: Shiliang was orphaned young and served his stepmother Lady Liang with a reputation for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he served his stepmother Lady Liang with renowned filial piety.

sentences.zh: 及卒，居喪合禮。

translations.literal: When she died he observed mourning in accord with the rites.
translations.idiomatic: At her death he mourned according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 文宣尋起令視事，士良屢表陳誠，再三不許，方應命。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan soon ordered him recalled to oversee affairs; Shiliang repeatedly memorialized his sincerity, and after three refusals was not permitted and only then accepted the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan soon ordered him back to duty; Shiliang refused three times before accepting.

sentences.zh: 文宣見其毀瘠，乃許之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenxuan saw how emaciated he was, he then permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how wasted he was, Wenxuan permitted the mourning.

sentences.zh: 因此臥疾歷年，文宣每自臨視。

translations.literal: Because of this he lay ill for years; Emperor Wenxuan personally came to visit him each time.
translations.idiomatic: He lay ill for years while Wenxuan visited him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 疾愈，除滄州刺史。

translations.literal: When his illness improved he was appointed inspector of Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When he recovered he became inspector of Cang.

sentences.zh: 乾明初，徵還鄴，授儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianming he was recalled to Ye and granted the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianming he was recalled to Ye and granted the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 孝昭即位，遣三道使搜揚人物。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhao took the throne he dispatched three groups of envoys to search out and recommend men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhao ascended the throne he sent three missions to seek out talent.

sentences.zh: 士良與尚書令趙郡王高睿、太常卿崔昂分行郡國，但有一介之善者，無不以聞。

translations.literal: Shiliang with Minister of the Secretariat Prince Gao Rui of Zhao commandery and Grand Master of Ceremonies Cui Ang traveled through commanderies and prefectures; wherever there was even the slightest good in a man, none failed to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang, with Minister Gao Rui of Zhao and Grand Master of Ceremonies Cui Ang, toured the provinces and reported every man of even slight merit.

sentences.zh: 齊武成初，除太子少傅、少師，復除侍中，轉太常卿，尋加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wucheng of Qi he was appointed Junior Tutor and Junior Teacher of the Heir Apparent, again made Palace Attendant, transferred to Grand Master of Ceremonies, and soon additionally granted the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Wucheng's reign he was Junior Tutor and Junior Teacher of the Heir Apparent, then Palace Attendant, Grand Master of Ceremonies, and soon granted the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 出為豫州道行台、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Commissioner-in-Chief of the Yuzhou Circuit and inspector of Yu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became circuit commissioner of Yuzhou and inspector of Yu.

sentences.zh: 子德衡，大象末，儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: His son Deheng, at the end of Daxiang, held the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies and the rank of Great General.
translations.idiomatic: His son Deheng, late in Daxiang, held the ceremonial regalia of the Three Excellencies and the rank of Great General.

sentences.zh: 論曰：昔陽貨外叛，庶其竊邑，而《春秋》譏之；

translations.literal: The commentary says: In old times Yang Huo rebelled abroad, hoping perhaps to seize a city, yet the Spring and Autumn Annals censured him;
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: When Yang Huo rebelled abroad, hoping to seize a city, the Spring and Autumn Annals censured him;

sentences.zh: 韓信背項，陳平歸漢，而史遷美之。

translations.literal: Han Xin turned against Xiang Yu and Chen Ping returned to Han, yet Sima Qian praised them.
translations.idiomatic: when Han Xin deserted Xiang Yu and Chen Ping joined Han, Sima Qian praised them.

sentences.zh: 蓋以運屬既安，君道已著，則徇利忘德者罪也；

translations.literal: Generally, when the age's destiny is already settled and the ruler's way is already manifest, then those who pursue profit and forget virtue are guilty;
translations.idiomatic: When the times are settled and the ruler's way is clear, those who trade virtue for profit are guilty;

sentences.zh: 時逢擾攘，臣禮未備，則轉禍為福者可也。

translations.literal: when the time meets turmoil and ministerial rites are not yet complete, then those who turn calamity into fortune may do so.
translations.idiomatic: when the realm is in turmoil and ministerial duty is unsettled, those who turn disaster to advantage may be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 崔彥穆、楊纂、段永等昔在山東，沈渝下位，並以羈旅之士，邅回于燕雀之伍，終佩龜組，可謂見機者乎？

translations.literal: Cui Yanmu, Yang Zuan, Duan Yong, and the like were formerly in Shandong, sunk in low positions, all men of the traveling guest—wandering among sparrows and swallows—yet in the end they wore tortoise seals; one may call them men who saw the moment, may one not?
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yanmu, Yang Zuan, and Duan Yong had languished in low posts east of the mountains as wandering strangers, yet in the end wore official seals—were they not men who seized their moment?

sentences.zh: 令狐整幹用確然，雅望重於河右，處州裏則勳著方隅，升朝廷則績宣出內，而畏避權寵，克保終吉，不然，何以自致顯名而取高位也？

translations.literal: Ling Huzheng's executive talent was solid, his refined standing weighty in the lands west of the Yellow River; in his prefecture and township his merit shone in the border regions, and ascending the court his achievements were proclaimed within and without—yet he feared and avoided power and favor and was able to preserve a good end to the last; otherwise, how could he by himself achieve a famous name and take a high position?
translations.idiomatic: Ling Huzheng was solid in action and eminent in the west; locally he secured the borders, at court he served within and without, yet shunned power and kept a good end—otherwise how could he have risen so high?

sentences.zh: 熙曆職流譽，風政克舉，雖古之循吏，亦何以加茲，而毫釐為爽，丘山成過，唯命也夫！

translations.literal: Xi in successive posts left a flowing reputation and his customs and administration could be raised up; though ancient conscientious officials could not surpass this, yet a hair's breadth of deviation made a hill of fault—only fate!
translations.idiomatic: Xi won flowing praise in every post and governed like the ancient conscientious officials, yet a hair's breadth of error became a mountain of blame—such is fate.

sentences.zh: 唐永良能之名，所在著美，清白之譽，顯於累職，所謂幹能之士也。

translations.literal: Tang Yong's name for ability and goodness was established wherever he was; his reputation for purity and whiteness shone through successive posts—he was what is called a man of ability and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yong's name for ability and integrity shone in every office—truly a man of talent and capacity.

sentences.zh: 瑾、敏並挺郐巳梓之林，蘊瑚璉之器，博觀載籍，多識舊章，固乃國之名臣，時之領袖，周無君子，斯焉取斯。

translations.literal: Jin and Min both stood in forests of timber from other states, harboring vessels of coral and jade, read widely in the written records, and knew many old regulations—in truth they were famous ministers of the state and leaders of the age; had Zhou lacked gentlemen, from where would it have taken them?
translations.idiomatic: Jin and Min were timber from beyond their homelands, vessels of jade in learning and law—state ministers and leaders of their age; without such men, whither would Zhou have turned?

sentences.zh: 王士良之仕于齊，職居卿牧，而失忠與義，臨難苟免，其背叛之徒歟！

translations.literal: Wang Shiliang in serving Qi held posts among the ministers and prefects, yet lost loyalty and righteousness and at difficulty sought only to escape—was he not one of the rebellious sort!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shiliang served Qi as minister and prefect yet abandoned loyalty in peril and sought only escape—was he not a turncoat?
